Hi Sophie — appreciate the heads up and the forecast. We can support a short, high‑intensity window; below is a pragmatic, fast path we can do without a full contract amendment. Please see proposed terms and next steps: 

Summary (fast path):
- Temporary headroom: enable burst pool capacity up to 4x your baseline for a 72‑hour window (must set exact start/end times)
- Billing: overrun is billed at a temporary discounted blended overrun rate of $0.018 per token for the first 48 hours, then $0.025 per token thereafter for any additional overrun beyond the uplift allocation
- Grace/Cap: we will cap total overrun charges for the 72‑hour event at $25,000 (one‑time cap) if uplift is requested by 24 hours prior to start; without 24‑hour notice the cap lowers to $15,000
- Credit: one‑time launch credit of $5,000 applied to your next invoice if you accept the uplift and run the event through Redwood (this is to offset integration ops risk)
- Proration & true‑up: usage will be prorated to the event window and reconciled on the next monthly invoice. Laura will outline the invoice presentation and math below.

Next steps:
1) Confirm desired start/end UTC times and whether you can provide the 24‑hour notice window.
2) If accepted, sign the quick amendment (DocuSign). I’ll flag Karthik to prioritize provisioning and Laura to prepare the invoice language.

If you prefer a different pricing shape (flat uplift fee vs per‑token overrun), tell me; we can convert to a blended uplift surcharge instead.

On urgency — we can provision without a signed amendment for one emergency activation, but to get the $25k cap and the $5k credit we need the signed DocuSign by EOD tomorrow.

—Markus

Hi Sophie — adding billing detail so your finance team has clarity. Key points on how the uplift and overrun will show up on your invoice: 

1) Allocation and billing windows
- We’ll provision a temporary uplift allocation (token allotment) for the exact start/end times you confirm. That allocation is billed pro rata for the billing month at your current committed rate (no uplift surcharge for the allocation itself).

2) Overrun charging (what happens if you exceed the uplift allocation)
- OverrunCharge = (ActualEventUsage - Allocation) * OverrunRate
- For this event we will apply the rate schedule Markus proposed: $0.018/token for the first 48 hours of overrun, then $0.025/token thereafter.
- The $25,000 cap (or $15,000 if <24h notice) is applied to the OverrunCharge total for the event.

3) Proration & true‑up presentation
- The uplift allocation will appear as a prorated line item on the month’s invoice (description: "Temporary uplift — Jul 17–19: X tokens allocated").
- Overrun will appear on the same invoice as a distinct line item ("Overrun — Jul 17–19: Y tokens at $Z/token"). We will include a small reconciliation table in the invoice PDF showing Allocation, Actual, Rate, and FinalCharge so your team can reconcile quickly.

4) Credits and timeline
- The $5,000 launch credit will be listed as a credit memo on the following invoice after the event; it is conditional on the signed DocuSign amendment if you want the $25,000 cap.

5) How we calculate tokens in bursts
- For the event we’ll use our standard token metering (input + output tokens) aggregated hourly and then summed for the event window. If you want line‑item hourly export for postmortem we can provide that as a CSV attachment to the invoice.

I’ve attached the proposed temporary uplift terms PDF that Karthik and Markus referenced (proposed_temp_uplift_terms.pdf). If that layout works we can generate the DocuSign today.

Laura Bennett
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
